sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: IL-KHANIDS
sources.note: Direct scholarly headword read: opening, geography, around 1260 to 1335, Hulegu foundation. Index years 1279 to 1400 are independently decoded map coverage.

sources.title: Reuven Amitai: Il-khanids, dynastic history
sources.note: Direct full scholarly article read. Dynastic history paragraphs on 1256, Baghdad 1258, paper money 1294, Abu Said 1335; institutional paragraphs on campaigns and fragmentation. The article contains a 1223 typo for the peace treaty, corrected internally later to 1323; neither treaty date is used here.

sources.title: Reuven Amitai: Ghazan Khan, Mahmud
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read: 17 June 1295 conversion; persecution and relaxation; taxation reform paragraphs explicitly assess Rashid al-Din as interested witness.

sources.title: Sheila S. Blair: Rab-e Rashidi
sources.note: Direct scholarly study read, based on the surviving deed dated 9 August 1309 and appendices. Architectural arrangement, personnel, bread rations, enslaved labour and charity. Draft describes deed provisions, not a population census.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Drugs
sources.note: Direct scholarly article, The Mongols and Timurids: Monday and Thursday dispensary, prescriptions and supervision. Cites Rashid al-Din 1977 pages 146 to 147. No claim of modern medical effectiveness.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World: Rab-i-Rashidi endowment deed
sources.note: Direct UNESCO record read, copying as protection against destruction, paper mill/library and institutional facilities. Page title says 13th century, but the dated 1309 deed is established by Blair; title date is not adopted.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: The Legacy of Genghis Khan, courtly art in western Asia
sources.note: Direct institutional exhibition text read: illustrated histories, political recasting of Iranian heroes, portable textiles and East Asian designs. Broad peaceful-era and first-ever world-history claims are not adopted.

sources.title: George Saliba: Tusi as mathematician and astronomer
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read. Independent mathematical works: dust-board arithmetic apparently completed in 1264; observatory and hay’a research: construction 1259, operational about 1261 to 1262. No unqualified claim about economic motives or Copernican transmission.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Soltaniyeh
sources.note: Direct indexed institutional statement read: mausoleum 1302 to 1312, 50-metre dome, double shell, eight minarets, turquoise faience. No claim that its design directly caused European architecture.

sources.title: British Museum: dated Ilkhanid frieze tile 1878,1230.575
sources.note: Direct collection catalogue read: Kashan fritware, moulded letters, lotus/peony, date 1 Shaban 709 / 4 January 1310. Exact Arabic Roman transliteration and translation in Inscriptions. Great Mosque Isfahan provenance is a curator’s suggestion, not confirmed findspot.

proposedOverrides.name: Ilkhanate
proposedOverrides.summary: A Mongol dynasty ruled Iran, Iraq and neighbouring regions; central power fragmented in 1335, before the imported map interval ends.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact existing indexed identity, no aliases or new geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Index 1279 to 1400 circa. Historical formation during Hulagu campaigns from 1256 and around 1260 consolidation; central dynastic collapse 1335. Public opening/ending explicitly distinguish imported interval from political lifetime.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two Historical Basemaps snapshots, 1279 to 1300 and 1300 to 1400, have the same broad bounding box [35.814958149581514,23.8803223141432,69.82449824498246,42.62114915688818]. Western Asia outline includes Iran, Mesopotamia, southern Caucasus/Anatolia areas. It is not a year-specific survey; public opening identifies broad outline. Full decoded features retained in parent identity-all-snapshots.json.
batchIdentityNotes.override: Retain map dates; dateBasis map_coverage, fell null and no successors because target identity/year/geometry navigation is not separately verified. No geometry correction claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: British Museum dated tile 1878,1230.575, exact brief Arabic transliteration and English translation; date from full inscription. Source prints Roman transliteration, not usable Arabic text, so no original glyphs reconstructed.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: Rab-e Rashidi details are provisions of 1309 endowment plus appendices, not universal household customs or population census. UNESCO heading misdates manuscript to thirteenth century, so dated Blair study controls chronology. Foundation used enslaved labour; identified plainly. Isfahan tile provenance remains proposed.
